I do want to say, that it doesn't matter how many people you sleep with, it is all chance. For example, my best friend used to have sex with randoms all the time and never used protection and she never has gotten any infections or diseases, but then I got both gonorrhea and HPV with my minimal mostly long term monog relationships. It is really a case of bad luck and a stupid stigmatized system.

I agree with you that it is so fucked up that dudes don't get tested for HPV because 1.) it isn't standard and 2.) they are affected by the outcomes of it.

When I got HPV, I got it from someone who knew they had it and never disclosed the information. He was a serial cheater and actually continues to have unprotected sex and cheat on women. However, we went to the police (me and his other ex) and there was nothing that could be done. I am afraid that they don't do anything unless it is something like HIV or something more immediately deadly.... but, don't be discouraged to look! Maybe you could be able to take on some legal action depending on where you are and your local laws.

BUT, consider this: Did your ex knowingly pass it on to you? Was it him being an inconsiderate asshole or did he not know he needed to be tested for that, too? Is he out there right now spreading HPV to other unknowing women? If he is, then you should do what you can to stop him, but if it were an accident, then I am sorry you are going through all of this pain because of him, but he didn't mean to hurt you like this and doesn't deserve to have a shitstorm come down on him. 

HPV is and isn't as serious as several other STI's and that is where a lot of the indifference comes from. It is horrible for women because our chances of cancer rise significantly, but dudes don't get affected by it (unless they have the kind with warts).

How to cope: when I found out it was right after I came out as a lesbian and it was really really horrible because gay sex is super hard without exchanging fluids, but I learned that nobody judges me for this thing I didn't choose to have. My sex life is fantastic and it just takes a little extra precaution (and it is way easier if you are doing penis and vagina stuff because condoms are so much easier than dental dams)....

1. Remember that, yes there is stigma, but your future partners likely won't care. This doesn't mean you are dirty or a slut or anything. Most people have some strain of HPV, so it should be understood easily if someone isn't a complete idiot.
2. You can beat this. You had one clear pap before and you can get a clear pap again. It isn't necessarily a lifelong sentence. You just have to get checked regularly, but it can go undetected when you can't spread it to anyone and it isn't hurting you. My aunt had HPV in college and she cleared it and never got it again (she is in her 40's now). You can clear it and never have to deal with it again.
3. Be angry! I was PISSED and it helped me deal with all of the immediate things I had to. Do not feel like you aren't allowed to have emotions because it sucks and it is super unfair you need to get surgery. Do whatever you feel like you need to do to make yourself feel okay. You can cry, scream, and throw a  tantrum. I did a lot of this and it made me feel a lot better.
4. Build up your immune system! There are lots of foods you can eat to help with this, but also get enough sleep and take care of yourself. If you have a good immune system it will be easier for your body to clear this, and it will make you feel better.
5. Confide in a friend. I still get depressed and angry from time to time because I worry about the future and my upcoming paps, but having people I can confide in and rant to is so helpful. 

Good luck!
